description: WebSocket message vectors. Spec: docs/protocol.md, "Control channel: WebSocket". valid[] and invalid[] cases are independent; sequences[] run in order on one connection that starts before hello.
howToRead: from = sender role (phone or pc), to = receiver role. state = "before_hello" (receiver has not seen a hello yet) or "open". Input is one of: frame (a JSON object, serialize compactly), raw (a text frame, send exactly this string), rawHex (a text frame with exactly these payload bytes, hex), binaryHex (a binary frame), synthesize ({ base, field, fill, fillCount, totalBytes }: take base, set base[field] to fill repeated fillCount times, serialize compactly in key order; the result is exactly totalBytes UTF-8 bytes). expect.reply = ack (receiver sends { type: ack, ref: frame.id }) | error (receiver sends { type: error, code, ref } and ref is omitted when null) | none. expect.close = WebSocket close code the receiver then uses, or null to stay open. expect.action is the category of what the receiver does: handshake_ok, mark_delivered, mark_failed, show_error_only, deliver_text, set_clipboard, start_download, mark_transfer_done, cancel_transfer, remove_peer_and_close, show_ping_toast, ignore_duplicate, close_only. raw may hold escapes that a JSON value cannot express (duplicate keys, lone surrogate escapes such as the six characters backslash u d 8 0 0): send the string exactly as written. expect.ref on an ack pins the id the ack points at. expect.sensitive on a deliver_text case says whether the receiver treats the text as sensitive (the optional sensitive field is true); absent means false. timers[] and closeCodes[] are about time and client behaviour, not frames: see their own fields. A closeCodes[] case may also carry helloAcceptedForMs (how long the peer's hello had been accepted when the connection ended, null if none ever was) and resetsBackoff (true only from 60000 ms on): the backoff resets only after a connection stayed open with an accepted hello for at least 60 s. raw cases named strict-* and nesting-* are invalid JSON for the protocol (unquoted literals, 01, NaN, nesting deeper than 64): bad_request with no ref.

valid.name: hello-unknown-platform-accepted
valid.note: any non-empty platform string is accepted

valid.name: hello-extra-fields-ignored
valid.note: unknown fields must be accepted and ignored

frame.message: Not enough free space on the phone.

valid.name: error-without-ref
valid.note: ref is optional; absent when the offending message had no usable id

valid.name: error-null-ref-is-absent
valid.note: null for an optional field means absent

frame.text:
line1
line2	"quoted" \ back é 日本 😀

valid.name: text-extra-fields-ignored
valid.note: unknown fields may hold any JSON, even non-integers

valid.name: text-id-not-a-uuid
valid.note: any non-empty string up to 64 characters is a valid id

valid.name: text-id-non-ascii
valid.note: ids are opaque; length counts code points

valid.name: text-id-64-astral-code-points
valid.note: 64 code points = 128 UTF-16 units; still valid

valid.name: offer-raw-names-are-not-cleaned-here
valid.note: the offer carries raw names (even empty); cleaning happens when the receiver saves (file-names.json)

valid.name: offer-total-size-mismatch-accepted
valid.note: totalSize is informational and is not validated

valid.name: offer-large-size
valid.note: 2^53-1 is the largest allowed integer

valid.name: offer-800-files-is-the-limit
valid.note: 800 files in one offer is allowed: the PC sends at most this many, and a bigger send is split into several offers

valid.name: cancel-any-reason-string
valid.note: reason is any string, including empty

valid.name: unpair-from-phone
valid.note: ack first, then remove the sender from devices and close with 1000

valid.name: text-frame-exactly-1-MiB
valid.note: a text frame of exactly 1,048,576 bytes (compact JSON, UTF-8) is accepted

valid.name: text-frame-multibyte-under-limit
valid.note: the limit counts UTF-8 bytes of the whole frame, not characters

valid.name: cancel-reason-error-from-phone
valid.note: a download file that fails for good (404 or 409) makes the phone cancel the whole transfer with reason error

valid.name: duplicate-keys-last-wins
valid.note: the last value of a repeated key wins: this is a text message with id last-id. A parser that keeps the first value would see a ping with no sentAt. Parse into a generic tree first, then validate

valid.name: duplicate-keys-last-wins-bad-first-value
valid.note: the earlier values (an empty text, a string for isUrl) are shadowed by the later ones, so the message is valid

valid.name: text-valid-surrogate-pair-escape
valid.note: an escaped surrogate PAIR is a normal character

valid.name: nesting-depth-64-in-an-unknown-field
valid.note: the top-level object plus 63 arrays is exactly 64 levels: valid (an unknown field may hold anything that is valid JSON)

valid.name: brackets-inside-strings-do-not-count-as-nesting
valid.note: the depth is counted on the structure of the JSON, not on bracket characters inside a string

valid.name: text-sensitive-true
valid.note: expect.sensitive is what the receiver treats the text as (absent in a case means false)

valid.name: text-sensitive-null-is-absent
valid.note: null for an optional field counts as absent

valid.name: text-sensitive-with-url-keeps-both-flags
valid.note: the receiver still gets isUrl true; it shows no preview and no Open action because the text is sensitive

invalid.name: first-message-is-not-hello
invalid.note: error, then close with 1002

invalid.name: first-message-unknown-type-before-hello
invalid.note: the before-hello check comes before the unknown-type check

invalid.name: first-message-not-json-before-hello
invalid.note: invalid JSON is step 2, before the hello check: bad_request, and the connection stays open (the 10 second timer still runs)

invalid.name: hello-protocol-2
invalid.note: error with ref = hello id, then close with 4002

invalid.name: hello-protocol-float
invalid.note: 1.0 is not an integer literal

invalid.name: hello-name-null
invalid.note: null for a required field is invalid

invalid.name: text-id-is-number
invalid.note: the id is not a usable string, so ref is left out

invalid.name: clipboard-from-phone-wrong-direction
invalid.note: clipboard is PC to phone only

invalid.name: offer-801-files-is-too-large
invalid.note: over the limit of 800 files the receiver rejects the offer: an error, no ack, nothing remembered (so a smaller offer with the same id is fine)

invalid.name: offer-file-size-above-2-pow-53
invalid.note: 2^53 is over the limit of 2^53-1

invalid.name: offer-transfer-id-with-slash
invalid.note: transfer IDs end up in URL paths, so they are limited to A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ (ref is still the id as sent)

invalid.name: cancel-old-shape-without-transferId
invalid.note: the pre-2026-10-14 shape (id = transfer id, no transferId) is no longer valid

invalid.name: ping-sentAt-float-literal
invalid.note: a number written with a fraction is not an integer, even if the value is whole

invalid.name: error-missing-code
invalid.note: error messages have no id, so ref in the reply is absent

invalid.name: unknown-type-is-checked-before-fields
invalid.note: step 5 (type) comes before step 6 (fields)

invalid.name: frame-trailing-garbage
invalid.note: the whole frame must be one JSON value

invalid.name: text-frame-1-MiB-plus-1-byte
invalid.note: one byte over 1,048,576: no reply at all, the connection is closed with 1009

invalid.name: text-frame-multibyte-over-limit
invalid.note: about 524,000 characters, but over 1 MiB in UTF-8 bytes

invalid.name: binary-frame-containing-valid-json
invalid.note: a binary frame is rejected even when its bytes are valid JSON

invalid.name: text-frame-invalid-utf8
invalid.note: rawHex is the exact frame payload bytes

invalid.name: first-message-json-without-type-before-hello
invalid.note: not a JSON object with a string type: bad_request, the connection stays open (the 10 second timer still runs)

invalid.name: first-message-ping-before-hello
invalid.note: a JSON object with a string type that is not hello: bad_request and the close with 1002

invalid.name: first-message-wrong-direction-before-hello
invalid.note: step 4 (before hello) comes before step 5 (direction)

invalid.name: hello-protocol-2-other-fields-missing
invalid.note: a future hello may look different: protocol is read before name, platform and appVersion

invalid.name: hello-protocol-2-without-id
invalid.note: no usable id, so ref is left out

invalid.name: hello-protocol-2-while-open
invalid.note: a later hello is checked the same way

invalid.name: hello-protocol-string-other-fields-missing
invalid.note: protocol is not a valid integer, so there is no version to compare: bad_request

invalid.name: hello-protocol-1-other-fields-missing-is-bad-request
invalid.note: protocol 1 is fine, so validation goes on to the other fields

invalid.name: text-lone-high-surrogate-escape
invalid.note: a lone surrogate escape makes the whole text invalid JSON: no ref even though the id is fine

invalid.name: lone-surrogate-escape-in-a-key
invalid.note: keys count too

invalid.name: strict-unquoted-literal-in-known-field
invalid.note: kotlinx parseToJsonElement probably accepts yes as an unquoted literal even in strict mode. strict JSON: not a valid literal, so the whole text is invalid JSON and gets bad_request with no ref (even though the id is fine)

invalid.name: strict-unquoted-literal-in-unknown-field
invalid.note: strict JSON: not a valid literal, so the whole text is invalid JSON and gets bad_request with no ref (even though the id is fine)

invalid.name: strict-capitalised-boolean-in-known-field
invalid.note: strict JSON: not a valid literal, so the whole text is invalid JSON and gets bad_request with no ref (even though the id is fine)

invalid.name: strict-leading-zero-in-known-field
invalid.note: 01 is not an integer literal: invalid JSON, not a ping with sentAt 1

invalid.name: strict-unquoted-literal-before-hello
invalid.note: invalid JSON is step 2, before the hello check: bad_request, the connection stays open

invalid.name: nesting-depth-65-in-an-unknown-field
invalid.note: the top-level object plus 64 arrays is 65 levels: invalid JSON, so bad_request with no ref (the id d65 is fine)

invalid.name: nesting-depth-65-before-hello
invalid.note: same rule before hello: bad_request, the connection stays open

invalid.name: nesting-depth-1000
invalid.note: far too deep: the depth must be counted before a recursive parser can overflow its stack

invalid.name: nesting-depth-65-in-a-field-an-offer-knows
invalid.note: unknown for a text message, but a known field name for an offer: the depth limit applies everywhere

sequences.name: handshake-then-text-then-duplicate
sequences.note: a repeat of an id gets the same ack and is not processed again

sequences.name: rejected-message-id-is-not-remembered
sequences.note: an invalid message is not processed, so the same id may be sent again with a corrected body

sequences.name: second-hello-after-handshake-is-a-normal-message
sequences.note: a hello is only special as the first message; later it is just a known type (no ack, no dedup)

sequences.name: invalid-hello-does-not-count-as-accepted
sequences.note: a hello that fails validation leaves the receiver before hello, so the next non-hello closes with 1002

sequences.name: garbage-before-hello-keeps-the-connection-open
sequences.note: first frames that are not a JSON object with a string type get bad_request and the connection stays open; a good hello then works

sequences.name: future-hello-gets-unsupported-version-not-a-timeout
sequences.note: protocol 2 with a different shape is answered with unsupported_version and 4002 straight away

sequences.name: same-pc-repeat-after-done-is-acked
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same paired PC repeats an offer whose download is DONE (the phone finished it, its complete may not have been acked, and the PC re-sent its queue after a reconnect). It is a repeat whatever the state of the download: the phone answers with the first response, the stored ack, downloads nothing again, and re-sends its complete if that was not acked. It is not bad_request

steps.note: the connection died; the PC never saw the ack, so it re-sends the offer after its hello

sequences.name: same-pc-repeat-after-canceled-is-acked
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same repeat for an offer that was CANCELED or FAILED on the phone: acked with the first response, nothing downloaded, and the phone re-sends its cancel (it keeps it until it is acked). Never bad_request

sequences.name: offer-from-another-device-is-bad-request
sequences.note: changelog 52: an offer with the ID of an offer that ANOTHER paired PC made is a reuse: error bad_request with ref = the offer id, and nothing is started. A transfer ID belongs to the device that made it. The first PC can still repeat its own offer afterwards

steps.note: a connection from a second paired PC

sequences.name: same-pc-repeat-with-different-files-is-bad-request
sequences.note: changelog 52, optional: a repeat from the same PC that lists other fileIds or other sizes than the first offer is not a repeat of it: error bad_request with ref = the offer id (the stored list stays). Names and MIME types are not compared. A receiver may skip this check

sequences.name: complete-re-sent-after-reconnect-is-acked-again
sequences.note: changelog 52: a complete is kept until it is acked and sent again, with the same message id, after every hello. The PC (which receives complete) acks the repeat with the first answer and does not mark the transfer done twice

steps.note: the ack of the complete was lost

sequences.name: cancel-re-sent-after-reconnect-is-acked-again
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same for a cancel, from either side: kept until acked, sent again with the same message id after every hello, and the receiver acks the repeat with its first answer without cancelling twice

steps.note: the ack of the cancel was lost

sequences.name: offer-reusing-a-text-id-is-bad-request
sequences.note: the ID space is shared: an offer whose id was already used by another message (a text here) is a reuse, not a repeat of that text, and gets error bad_request with ref = the offer id. The text is not acked or delivered a second time

sequences.name: offer-repeated-while-unfinished-is-acked-after-a-reconnect
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same paired PC re-offers an offer that is not over (it re-sent its queue, because the ack never reached it): acked as a repeat, and the phone carries on with that download. A repeat after the download is over is acked too: see same-pc-repeat-after-done-is-acked

steps.note: the connection died before the PC saw the ack; the PC reconnects and sends its queue again

sequences.name: queue-resend-after-reconnect-is-idempotent
sequences.note: a queued text is re-sent with the same id after a reconnect: the receiver repeats its first ack and does not deliver it twice. The queue goes out in creation order (A, B, C)

steps.note: the ack of B was lost: no ack in 5 s, so B goes back to queued

sequences.name: queue-is-not-sent-before-hello
sequences.note: after a reconnect nothing else goes out before the hellos: a text before the hello is bad_request and the 1002 close, and its id is not remembered, so the queue sends it again on the next connection

steps.note: the 1002 close ended it; the next connection does the hellos first

timers.name: no-hello-10-and-a-half-seconds-closes-with-1002
timers.note: no error message is sent: the connection is just closed with 1002

timers.name: hello-accepted-then-silence-is-not-this-timers-business
timers.note: liveness after the handshake is WebSocket ping/pong, see the architecture

closeCodes.name: going-away-1001
closeCodes.note: not in the close table: handled like 1000

closeCodes.name: internal-error-1011
closeCodes.note: not in the close table: handled like 1000

closeCodes.name: protocol-error-1002-from-peer
closeCodes.note: the backoff stops a persistent bug from becoming a fast loop

closeCodes.name: replaced-4001
closeCodes.note: another connection took over this device: only reconnect on the next user action or network change

closeCodes.name: stable-60-s-then-network-error
closeCodes.note: the hello had been accepted for exactly 60 s: the backoff goes back to its first step

closeCodes.name: stable-an-hour-then-replaced-4001
closeCodes.note: it was a stable connection, so the backoff is reset even though no automatic reconnect follows

closeCodes.name: closed-at-once-after-an-accepted-hello
closeCodes.note: a peer that accepts the hello and closes at once must not turn the reconnect into a fast loop

closeCodes.name: no-hello-ever-accepted-1002
closeCodes.note: the 10 s hello timeout: the socket was open, but no hello was accepted, so it counts for nothing

closeCodes.name: open-10-minutes-but-hello-accepted-5-s-ago
closeCodes.note: the 60 s are counted from the accepted hello, not from the moment the socket opened
